transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m constantly hung up on how my face looks on camera and in person, and it’s making me avoid people and things I used to enjoy. It has just gotten to the point where it's taking over my life and I felt like I needed to get some help.

When you avoid people, is it mainly because you’re afraid they’ll judge your appearance, or because you feel down and have lost interest in being around others? Have you been spending a lot of time checking, hiding, or trying to fix the part of your face that bothers you?

It’s definitely because I’m terrified people are judging my crooked jaw and cheek scar, not because I’ve lost interest in being social. To try and cope, I constantly check my face in my phone camera, zoom in on the scar, take and delete dozens of selfies, and constantly fiddle with my beard or tilt my head to try and hide how lopsided I look.

Do you think your jaw and scar only look noticeably abnormal to you, or are you certain that other people can clearly see and judge them too? Has anyone else told you they don’t really notice what you’re seeing?

I’m absolutely convinced that everyone else notices and judges it, because to me, the asymmetry and the scar are just glaringly obvious. My girlfriend, my students, and a close friend have all reassured me that they don't see what I'm seeing, but I can't help but feel they're just saying that to be polite. No matter how much they reassure me, it still feels completely real to me.

Do you ever have moments when you think you might be exaggerating how noticeable your jaw and scar are, or are you completely certain your face looks abnormal to other people all the time? Have you ever changed your mind about that, even briefly?

Deep down, it feels completely real and I'm usually convinced that my crooked jaw and scar are highly noticeable to everyone. The only reason I agreed to seek help is because a close friend told me my worries were way out of proportion, but it is incredibly difficult to actually believe them when my face looks so obviously asymmetrical to me.

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (crooked jaw, cheek scar) that others reportedly do not notice or view as minimal, accompanied by repetitive appearance-related behaviors (mirror/camera checking, repeated selfies, grooming/camouflaging) and significant social avoidance/impairment. Insight is poor to absent, as the patient is largely convinced others can clearly see and judge the defect. This is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder under ICD-10 code F45.2.
